mainEntity.name: What does KRIVA build, and for whom?

acceptedAnswer.text: We design company websites, mobile apps, and custom software for US trucking, moving, and logistics businesses, and we also build B2B SaaS products and QuickBooks and Xero integrations. A website collects the quote. Software runs the desk after the job exists. They are separate projects.

mainEntity.name: Should we buy a TMS instead of building one?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. If your freight and workflows are standard, a boxed TMS will be cheaper and faster, and we will say so. Custom pays off when spreadsheets run your core decisions or your workflow is your edge. Our build vs buy guide covers how to decide.

mainEntity.name: How long does a project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Discovery takes 1 to 2 weeks. A six-page website is scheduled once your content is ready, and the proposal states the date. A focused product is usually 6 to 10 weeks, and a full platform with integrations usually runs 12 to 20 weeks.

mainEntity.name: How is pricing structured?

acceptedAnswer.text: Website, app, design, dashboard, and accounting work have published starting prices for a defined scope. Dispatch platforms and other custom software are quoted after discovery. Engagements run as fixed-scope projects, sprints, or a monthly retainer. Starting prices: https://krivatechnologies.com/pricing.

mainEntity.name: Can you change our system without stopping operations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. New screens run beside your current system behind feature flags, tested in staging and reviewed weekly, and they go live in phases once you sign off.

mainEntity.name: How do you work with US teams from India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our team is in Ahmedabad and overlaps with US and UK hours for calls and demos, with written updates in between. In-person meetings are not required.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the code and designs?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do. Figma files, repositories, and documentation transfer to you at project close or earlier, with no lock-in.

mainEntity.name: Do you sign NDAs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Mutual NDA available on request before sharing confidential project information.

@graph.name: KRIVA product design and development process
@graph.description: Five phases with a written next step: discover, design, build, launch, and optional support. Discover and design end with your sign-off.

step.name: Discover
step.text: Strategy, scope, users, constraints, and success metrics go into a written brief. The phase is 1 to 2 weeks and ends when you sign. You leave with a scoped brief and a realistic timeline.

step.name: Design
step.text: Flows, prototypes, and high-fidelity UI are reviewed in weekly demos over 2 to 5 weeks. Engineering does not start until you sign the pack. A later change is a change request.

step.name: Build
step.text: You see working software every week on a real URL. Regression checks run before each demo. A person still reviews what ships.

step.name: Launch
step.text: Deployment, analytics, handoff docs, and training. The product is not called live until the checklist is complete and someone on your side can operate it.

step.name: Support
step.text: Optional monthly retainer for iteration, automation maintenance, and roadmap support, or a clean handoff. Support is a choice, not a lock-in.

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Discovery is 1–2 weeks and ends with a brief you sign. Most scoped projects run 6–16 weeks. A larger SaaS platform with integrations can run 12–20 weeks. We do not quote a date until the brief is written. A fit call is for fit, not a timeline we cannot yet defend.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us?

acceptedAnswer.text: A named decision-maker, access to the people who will use the product, and feedback inside the weekly cadence. If the desk cannot join a demo, we will say the engagement is not ready.

mainEntity.name: How do timezones work?

acceptedAnswer.text: We work remote-first. The studio is in Ahmedabad, India, with overlap windows for UK and US clients. Demos sit in that overlap. Async notes go out the same day. You should not need midnight calls.

mainEntity.name: How is this different from AI-Assisted Development?

acceptedAnswer.text: This page is the delivery sequence: phases, gates, and cadence. AI-assisted development is how tools such as Claude, Copilot, and Cursor are used inside those phases. Tools speed the work. A person still signs what ships.

mainEntity.name: Do QuickBooks and Xero projects use the same process?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Finance connectors still get a written brief, a signed operator surface, weekly demos, and a go-live checklist. The write into QuickBooks Online or Xero uses the original APIs. The gates do not change.

mainEntity.name: What happens after launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can take the handoff and run it, or stay on a monthly retainer for iteration and automation maintenance. Support is Phase 05 and optional. It is not bundled as a surprise.

mainEntity.name: What services do you offer?

acceptedAnswer.text: We design and build trucking and logistics software - dispatch CRM , fleet dashboards, and driver apps - plus B2B SaaS ( onboarding, dashboards, MVPs ), QuickBooks and Xero integrations , and workflow automation . We focus on these areas because we have spent years on them.

mainEntity.name: Do you subcontract any work?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Every designer and engineer on your project is a permanent KRIVA team member. We do not use freelance marketplaces or offshore subcontractors. The team you meet on the first call is the team that builds your product.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with startups and enterprises?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. For startups, we are used to fast timelines, limited scope, and investor-facing deliverables. For scale-ups and enterprises, we are used to compliance requirements, complex integrations, and multi-stakeholder sign-off. We scope projects accordingly.

mainEntity.name: Can you work with our existing team?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We embed with in-house designers, developers, or product managers and adapt to your tools and working style.

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A focused MVP or redesign is usually 6 to 10 weeks. A full-stack SaaS platform with integrations runs 12 to 20 weeks. Discovery sprints are 1 to 2 weeks. We give an honest timeline on the first call. See our delivery process for how phases and sign-off gates work.

mainEntity.name: How do you use AI in your delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: We use Claude for content and brief drafting, GitHub Copilot for code generation, Cursor for rapid prototyping, and Figma AI for asset generation. Every output is reviewed by a senior team member before it reaches you. AI makes us faster; people make sure it is right.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the design files and code after the project?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do. All Figma files, GitHub repositories, and documentation transfer to you at project close, or earlier if you prefer. No lock-in or vendor dependency. We help onboard your internal team on what we built.

mainEntity.name: How is pricing structured?

acceptedAnswer.text: Website, app, design, dashboard, and accounting work have published starting prices at https://krivatechnologies.com/pricing for a defined scope. Dispatch platforms and other custom software are quoted after discovery. Engagements run as fixed-scope projects, monthly retainers, or sprint-based work.

mainEntity.name: What happens after launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: After go-live you can move to a monthly retainer: iteration sprints, performance monitoring, and roadmap support. You can scale the retainer up or pause it as needed. We do not vanish after handoff.

mainEntity.name: Where are you based, and how do remote work and time zones work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Headquarters is in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. The studio is remote-first: we overlap call hours with the US, UK, UAE, and Canada, work async between those windows, and align stand-ups to your team’s schedule. In-person meetings are not required.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us to get started?

acceptedAnswer.text: A brief ( we will send a template ), your timeline, and a 20-minute fit call. If you do not have a brief yet, we will write one together. Many teams arrive with a problem, not a spec.

mainEntity.name: Do you sign NDAs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Mutual NDA available on request before sharing confidential project information.

mainEntity.name: Should we buy a TMS instead of building one?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. If your freight and workflows are standard, a boxed TMS will be cheaper and faster, and we will say so on the call. Custom software pays off when spreadsheets run your core decisions or your workflow is your edge. Many teams keep the TMS as the record and build the desk tools around it.

mainEntity.name: How do you handle quality assurance?

acceptedAnswer.text: QA runs inside every build sprint. Regression checks run before each weekly demo, integrations are tested against staging with sanitized data, and launch has a go-live checklist your team signs off.

mainEntity.name: How do you approach security?

acceptedAnswer.text: We scope role-based access and audit trails into the product where you need them, verify signed webhooks on integrations that support them. Mutual NDA available on request before sharing confidential project information. If you need a specific certification or compliance evidence from your vendors, raise it on the fit call so we can tell you plainly whether we can meet it.

mainEntity.name: Can you connect to our ELD, TMS, or accounting software?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually, where the provider offers an API or data export. We build QuickBooks Online and Xero integrations on their public APIs, and we check what your ELD or TMS provider allows during discovery rather than assuming it.

mainEntity.name: Do you have an office in the UAE?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. KRIVA is remote-first from Ahmedabad, India, and we do not claim a local presence we do not have. Gulf Standard Time is two and a half hours ahead of us, so a normal UAE working day overlaps almost entirely with ours - in practice that means same-day replies and live sessions at ordinary hours for both sides.

mainEntity.name: Can you build Arabic and English in the same product?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is much cheaper to plan for at the start. We structure layouts, components, and content for bidirectional text from the wireframe stage. Translation itself is usually handled by your team or a translation partner; what we own is making sure the interface does not break when the direction flips.

mainEntity.name: Which accounting systems can you integrate with?

acceptedAnswer.text: QuickBooks and Xero are the two we work with most, using their official APIs. For regional ERPs and bank feeds we work against whatever documented API exists, and we say plainly when a system has no viable integration path rather than building a fragile scraper.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the code and the designs?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do. Repositories, Figma files, and documentation transfer to you at close or earlier if you prefer. There is no licensing arrangement and no lock-in to us for future work.

mainEntity.name: Can you work with our existing TMS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, that's the most common path. We keep your TMS as the source of record when that makes sense and build dispatch consoles, driver apps, or portals connected through its API, EDI, or file exchange, scoped in discovery.

mainEntity.name: Do we need to replace our current software?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often no. Many projects tune gaps, add a console beside the TMS, or replace one module at a time. Full replacement is an option when spreadsheets run dispatch, exceptions surface too late, or the architecture cannot support your model.

mainEntity.name: Can you build a custom dispatch workflow?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We map assignment, bulk actions, exceptions, and supervisor overrides from how dispatch works today, then build the board or console around that, usually the first module we ship.

mainEntity.name: Can you connect accounting systems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Load-to-invoice workflows and reconciliation states can sync to QuickBooks or Xero, with retry visibility finance can trust, not silent drift between ops and books.

mainEntity.name: Can you build driver-facing software?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Driver and carrier apps for load acceptance, in-transit updates, and POD, with offline queue where yard signal is weak. Updates sync back to dispatch and your TMS.

mainEntity.name: Can you improve a spreadsheet-based workflow?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We map what the spreadsheet actually controls first, the queue, the SLA logic, the handoffs, then rebuild it as an audited board so nothing dispatch relies on gets lost in the transition.

mainEntity.name: Can we start with one workflow instead of rebuilding everything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Most engagements start with the highest-pain module, usually dispatch, and expand in whatever sequence carries the least operational risk. New surfaces run in parallel with phased cutover after operations signs off.

mainEntity.name: How long does a custom trucking software project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Discovery takes 1 to 2 weeks and ends with a scoped brief and timeline you sign off. A full project usually runs 6 to 16 weeks depending on scope, with working software on a live URL every week.

mainEntity.name: How much does custom dispatch or TMS software cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Custom software cost is team size multiplied by weeks, so it depends on how many surfaces and integrations are in scope. KRIVA quotes after discovery, broken into team, weeks, and phases, with exclusions listed.

mainEntity.name: Do you build ELD devices or replace our ELD provider?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. KRIVA builds software, not ELD hardware. Where your ELD or telematics provider offers an API or data export, we bring its location and hours-of-service data into dispatch views. What is available depends on the provider and is confirmed in discovery.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with early-stage and scaling SaaS teams?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We work with pre-seed MVPs through Series A and later scaling products. Team size and engagement model follow stage and runway, not a fixed package.

mainEntity.name: Can you redesign an existing SaaS product?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Redesigns ship in phases so current users keep a working path. We typically start with onboarding, roles, or the daily home rather than a full visual restyle.

mainEntity.name: Do you provide design-only and design-and-build engagements?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many teams start with product design and extend into engineering with the same in-house team. You choose the model.

mainEntity.name: Can you help define onboarding and activation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Before any screens, we name the user, the product job, and the event that means the product has actually been used. A finished setup checklist is not treated as that event.

mainEntity.name: Do you design multi-tenant roles and admin workflows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Safe default permissions, invitations, workspace access, and admin controls that stay understandable when SSO and policy arrive.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the final design files and source code?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do. Design files and source code transfer to your accounts. KRIVA does not subcontract; the team on the first call is the team that designs and builds.

mainEntity.name: How long does a SaaS MVP or redesign take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A focused MVP or redesign usually takes 6 to 10 weeks. A full SaaS platform with integrations runs 12 to 20 weeks. Both start with 1 to 2 weeks of discovery that ends in a scoped brief and timeline you sign off. See how we deliver.

mainEntity.name: How is pricing structured?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fixed-scope projects, monthly retainers, or sprint-based work. Everything is scoped after discovery, with deliverables and milestones agreed upfront, so you know the cost before the build starts.

mainEntity.name: How is this page different from SaaS platform design?

acceptedAnswer.text: This page covers the full product, from MVP through integrations. SaaS platform design focuses on multi-tenant admin and customer UX for products that are already live.

mainEntity.name: QuickBooks Desktop or QuickBooks Online?

acceptedAnswer.text: We build against QuickBooks Online through Intuit's public API. QuickBooks Desktop uses a different integration route and is not what this page covers; if you are on Desktop, tell us on the fit call and we will say plainly whether we can help. Xero is a cloud API only.

mainEntity.name: Can you sync both Xero and QuickBooks for different regions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Multi-region billing with separate connectors and a unified operator dashboard is a common SaaS pattern: QBO for US entities, Xero for UK, one exception queue.

mainEntity.name: How do you handle sync failures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every job logs errors, retries with backoff and source-record keys so a retry cannot double-post, and surfaces exceptions in an operator dashboard with a next step. Expired or revoked authorizations show up as a reconnect task, not a silent stall. Failures are visible before close, not after.

mainEntity.name: How is this different from your API integrations service?

acceptedAnswer.text: API integrations covers CRM, payments, ELD, and general connectors. This page is the finance-specific solution: QuickBooks, Xero, matching, the close, and the operator screens around exceptions. Many products need both.

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical integration take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A focused QBO or Xero connector with operator UX usually takes weeks, not days: mapping sign-off, a build against a sandbox, and a parallel run on live books. Production access also depends on Intuit's app assessment for QuickBooks and Xero's connection limits for new apps. Dual-region or multi-entity setups run longer. We give a real range on the first call, not a padded one.

mainEntity.name: Stripe or payment processor sync?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, as source events. Payments and payouts from a processor such as Stripe enter the same queue as invoices and are matched in the ledger. Building the payment connector itself is covered under API integrations; the matching and close screens are covered here.

mainEntity.name: What data can a QuickBooks or Xero integration sync?

acceptedAnswer.text: Typically invoices, payments, credit notes, customers or contacts, and the account, item, and tax codes they depend on. In QuickBooks Online that can include bills and vendors; in Xero, bank transactions and tracking categories. The exact list, and which system is the source of truth for each record, is agreed and signed off during data mapping.

mainEntity.name: How is pricing structured?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fixed-scope projects, monthly retainers, or sprint-based work. Everything is scoped after discovery, with deliverables and milestones agreed upfront, so you know the cost before the build starts. You own the code and documentation at handover.

mainEntity.name: What is auto transport software?

acceptedAnswer.text: Auto transport software runs the vehicle shipping workflow for brokers and car carriers: customer quotes and booking, carrier assignment and dispatch, driver condition reports and proof of delivery (POD), customer shipment tracking, and invoicing. A custom build keeps all of it on one order record instead of separate tools.

mainEntity.name: Can you improve our current platform without replacing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and that is where most engagements start. We map the quote-to-delivery journey first, find where orders leak into texts and spreadsheets, then recommend whether the fix is configuration, a connected tool, a redesign, or a rebuild.

mainEntity.name: Can this connect with our existing TMS, CRM, or accounting software?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually, where the system offers an API or data export. The order record connects through defined integrations, with visible validation errors, failed-sync states, and retries instead of silent drift. We confirm what each of your systems exposes during discovery, before anything is scoped.

mainEntity.name: Do you build quote engines and customer tracking?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We build itemized quote engines with pricing rules your team can adjust as routes, seasons, and fuel costs change, and customer tracking with status, ETA updates, and one shareable link per order.

mainEntity.name: Can the driver app work with weak or no signal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We design condition capture, signatures, and POD to work offline: updates queue on the phone when signal drops and sync when it returns, with clear states for what has sent and what is still pending.

mainEntity.name: How long does a custom auto transport software project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Discovery takes 1 to 2 weeks and ends with a scoped brief and timeline you sign off. A full project usually runs 6 to 16 weeks depending on scope, with working software on a live URL every week.

mainEntity.name: How much does custom auto transport software cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost depends on how many tools and integrations are in scope, so we quote after discovery, broken into team, weeks, and phases, with exclusions listed. Starting with one high-pain piece, such as the quote and booking portal, keeps the first phase small.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the final code and design files?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do. Designs, source code, and documentation transfer to your accounts at launch. Ongoing support is optional, with no lock-in.

mainEntity.name: Do you use AI to write our code and designs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Selectively. Tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Figma AI plugins help with drafting, refactoring, test scaffolding, and exploring options. Engineers and designers review everything and own what is merged or delivered. If your security policy or contract rules a tool out, tell us and we leave it out.

mainEntity.name: Can you add an AI feature to our dispatch or SaaS product?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for scoped jobs such as summarizing an exception, drafting a message, or pulling fields from a document into a review screen. We test on sanitized samples you provide and design the fallback for low-confidence results. We do not promise accuracy figures in advance, because they depend on your documents.

mainEntity.name: Will AI send messages to customers or carriers on its own?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not by default. AI drafts, a person approves, and the send step stays with your team. If you want one narrow, low-risk action to go automatically, we scope it with explicit rules, logging, and a way to turn it off.

mainEntity.name: What happens to our data when AI tools are involved?

acceptedAnswer.text: We ask before putting any client data into an AI tool, prefer sanitized samples, and check the tool's data terms with you before production use. Mutual NDA available on request before sharing confidential project information. For anything sensitive, an option is to keep AI out of that part of the workflow entirely.

mainEntity.name: How is this different from Automation Workflows?

acceptedAnswer.text: This page covers how AI is used to build your product and which AI features go inside it. Automation Workflows covers repeated ops steps in Make, Zapier, or custom code, with approval gates. The two overlap when an AI step sits inside an automated workflow.

mainEntity.name: Will automation message our customers or brokers on its own?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for anything that carries money, a commitment, or a complaint. Status copies, internal flags, and document filing can run without a person. A customer-facing message, a detention claim, or an invoice waits in an approval queue until someone on your team sends it. If you want one narrow message to go automatically, we scope it with explicit rules and an off switch.

mainEntity.name: Which steps should we automate first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with work that is repeated, rule-based, and cheap to get wrong: copying load status into a sheet, filing PODs against the right load, flagging a missed check call. Leave judgment calls, such as reassigning a late load or waiving detention, with your dispatchers and billing team. We confirm the list during the workflow map.

mainEntity.name: Make, Zapier, or custom code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Make or Zapier when the volume, connectors, and approval steps fit inside the platform and your team will maintain it. Custom workers when run limits, data handling, or the approval console outgrow the platform. We check run limits, connector coverage, and data terms before recommending one.

mainEntity.name: What if our TMS or load board has no API?

acceptedAnswer.text: It happens often. We read the vendor's API docs and your account permissions first. If there is no usable API, the fallbacks are scheduled exports, email parsing, or a small import step, each with more failure modes. If none of those is reliable enough, we will say the step should stay manual.

mainEntity.name: How is this different from Integrations & APIs and AI-Assisted Development?

acceptedAnswer.text: This service designs the queue: triggers, approvals, and what happens when a run fails. Integrations & APIs covers connector architecture between systems. AI-Assisted Development covers how AI is used to build and inside your product. We may use an LLM step inside a scenario, with a person approving the output.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the workflow after launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your team. The scenarios live in your Make, Zapier, or hosting accounts. We hand over the workflow map, naming, run-failure queue, and a short runbook. Ongoing changes can stay in-house, or we can agree a small support arrangement if you ask for one.

mainEntity.name: Should we customize our CRM or replace it?

acceptedAnswer.text: We assess first. If stages, permissions, and the CRM's own bulk actions already fit, configuration is the answer and nothing needs building. Replacement comes up only when the platform cannot support bulk work, role-based views, or audited overrides for the way your desk runs.

mainEntity.name: Will this replace our TMS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not by default. The TMS stays the system of record and the new console runs beside it, rolled out by role or module. If you want to retire a TMS module later, we scope that as a separate step.

mainEntity.name: Can the dispatch board work with our TMS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually, depending on what the TMS exposes. We check API access, export options, and your account permissions first. If there is no usable API, scheduled exports or an import step are the fallback, with more failure modes. We tell you before the build which case you are in.

mainEntity.name: Can you migrate data from a legacy CRM or spreadsheets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, when it is in scope. We map fields, run test imports on sanitized samples, and agree a cutover by role or module so the desk keeps working. Messy history sometimes needs a decision from your team about what to keep.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us to start?

acceptedAnswer.text: A day of watching the desk work, a sanitized export of recent loads or deals, sandbox or admin access to the CRM and TMS, and one person per role who can say whether a screen works for them.

mainEntity.name: What happens after launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Designs, code, and documentation transfer to your accounts. Changes after go-live can stay with your team, or we can agree a support retainer if you want one. We do not host your data unless we scope hosting as part of the project.

mainEntity.name: How long does a custom CRM project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Discovery takes 1 to 2 weeks and ends with a scoped brief and timeline you sign off. A focused first version, such as one console or one pipeline, is usually 6 to 10 weeks after that. A larger build with several integrations usually runs 12 to 20 weeks.

mainEntity.name: How much does custom CRM development cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost follows scope: team size multiplied by weeks. We price after discovery, as a fixed-scope project, sprints, or a monthly retainer. Our guide to custom dispatch software cost explains what drives the budget.

mainEntity.name: Can you improve a dashboard we already have?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. If your TMS or reporting tool lets us control layout and filters, we redesign inside it. If it does not, we say so and show what a custom view would cost in time. Either way we start by watching how the dashboard is used today.

mainEntity.name: Where does the data come from, and how fresh is it?

acceptedAnswer.text: From the systems you already run: the TMS, CRM, accounting tool, and telematics if the vendor offers an API. A dashboard is only as current as its slowest source, so we agree refresh timing per source and show "last updated" on screen. We do not promise live data we cannot get.

mainEntity.name: Can a dashboard replace our morning-scan spreadsheet?

acceptedAnswer.text: That is the most common reason people call. If the spreadsheet exists because filters and actions do not match the work, a redesigned view can retire it. ShiftRail is the example: the desk moved off a second sheet once exceptions and SLA sat on the board.

mainEntity.name: How do you decide what goes at the top?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each role gets one primary question, such as which loads will miss their appointment. The top of the screen answers that question and lets the user act. A chart that does not change a decision moves lower or goes away.

mainEntity.name: Do you only design, or also build?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are possible. Some teams want designs and specs for their own engineers; others want us to build the views too. We scope the data work separately because it is often the larger part.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us?

acceptedAnswer.text: Screenshots or exports of what people use today, access to the data sources or sample exports, and time with two or three people who use the dashboard daily. A named person who can settle disagreements between roles helps a lot.

mainEntity.name: Native, React Native, or Flutter for a driver app?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the job. Heavy camera use, background location, Bluetooth hardware, or strict battery limits can push toward native. A cross-platform framework often fits when the screens are mostly forms, status, and document capture. We make the call after the first workshop and write down why.

mainEntity.name: How does offline proof of delivery work?

acceptedAnswer.text: The app saves the photo or signature on the phone, shows it as queued, and retries when signal returns. The driver sees what has uploaded and what is still waiting, and dispatch sees the same state. We agree conflict rules with you, such as what happens if the load was reassigned while the phone was offline.

mainEntity.name: Can the app connect to our TMS or dispatch system?

mainEntity.name: Do you build the platform, or only design it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. One in-house team designs and engineers the tenant model, the admin and customer surfaces, and the APIs and integrations behind them, typically in Next.js, React, Node.js, and PostgreSQL. If your engineers prefer to write the code, we deliver the role model, designs, and component specs instead. Either way, you own the code and designs.

mainEntity.name: Can you change a live SaaS product without a big-bang cutover?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and phased is the default. New surfaces and permission checks ship behind feature flags, tested in staging, and roll out to pilot tenants first. Existing tenants keep working while the rest of the product moves over.

mainEntity.name: How do you keep one tenant's data away from another?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every record carries its tenant, and the API checks tenant and role on every read and write instead of relying on filters in the UI. We review where those rules are enforced today and agree the isolation model with your engineers before migrating anything.

mainEntity.name: Can you integrate SSO, subscriptions, and billing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We connect SSO sign-in to the role model, with a safe default role for new users, and build plan, seat, and billing screens inside the product. Subscription and payment events from Stripe or your billing system can post to QuickBooks Online or Xero with an exception queue for finance. We confirm the exact providers during discovery.

mainEntity.name: How is this different from SaaS product development?

acceptedAnswer.text: SaaS product development covers new products: MVP scope, onboarding, and activation. This service covers live platforms that already have tenants, roles, and billing, where the work is tenant isolation, permissions, and bringing admin and customer surfaces back into one product family.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us to start?

acceptedAnswer.text: Access to the live product or a staging copy, read access to the repository, your current role and permission list, a few sanitized tenant setups, and time with someone from support or customer success who hears where tenants get stuck.
